subject: ACME POC: integration plan & success criteria

Subject: ACME POC: post-call recap & proposed success criteria

Thanks again for your time this morning, Samantha — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before the technical kickoff:

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Inference for customer-facing chat assistant & knowledge search (low-latency generation + embeddings).
- Primary success metrics: 1) production-like latency under 95th% <= 300ms for single-turn generation (50–200 tokens), 2) embedding quality measured by Precision@5 on your test queries >= 0.75 vs current baseline, 3) stable throughput of ~40 reqs/s during peak scenario, and 4) no PII leakage in sampled prompts.

Proposed POC plan (2-week POC)
- Week 1: Integration & baseline runs (SDK integration, streaming tests, embeddings), sample prompts and eval dataset ingestion.
- Week 2: Load runs, quality evaluation (precision & human review), and final results + recommendation.

Ownership / roles
- ACME: Samantha (PM) + Tom (procurement) for access and purchase approvals.
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) – project owner; Vivek (SE) – technical lead; Rachel (CS) – onboarding + success.

Tech kickoff items (what Vivek will cover)
- SDK install and auth flow (API key + recommended usage patterns)
- API endpoints for generation, streaming, embeddings, and function/tool calling patterns
- Sample workload and guidance on batching and KV cache usage

Ask / next steps
1) Please confirm the success criteria above or share changes by EOD Fri.
2) Confirm we can schedule a 60-min tech kickoff next week (proposed: Mon 3/22 or Tue 3/23).
3) Provide an email for a test account or approve us to create a scoped test key.

Attached: ACME_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (draft)

Thanks,

Hi Samantha — happy to run the tech kickoff. Quick high-level implementation plan to address your questions so the kickoff can be focused and actionable:

1) SDK & auth - We have first-party SDKs (JS / Python). Auth is API key based for the POC; keys can be scoped to region and usage limits. For your frontend streaming use case we recommend issuing a short-lived key and proxying via your backend.

2) API routes (examples) - POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate — standard sync generation (request/response). - POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream — SSE/HTTP2 streaming for partial tokens (fits websocket bridge). - POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings — batch embeddings endpoint (supports up to 1024 items/batch). - POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/call — function/tool calling interface; supports schema-based tool descriptors and structured outputs.

3) Streaming -> Websocket pattern - Typical setup: frontend opens websocket to your backend -> backend opens SSE stream to our /v1/stream endpoint -> backend forwards partial tokens to frontend. This keeps API keys off the client and supports reconnect/resume. I’ll demo a nodejs example during the kickoff.

4) Tool calling and structured outputs - Our /v1/call endpoint supports function calling: you pass a JSON schema for tools and the model will return structured calls. SE tip: validate tool inputs server-side and include a short tool-execution sandbox for safety.

5) Performance tips for latency/cost - Use prefix caching for repeated system prompts, small batch sizes for low-latency single-turn traffic, and quantized model variants to reduce token processing time. We’ll provide recommended batching settings after seeing your token-size distribution.

6) Region & data residency - For the scoped POC we can pin logs and data retention to us-west (us) region. I’ll include the scoped test key config in the kickoff notes.

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf

I’ll prepare a short demo repo and a node/python snippet for streaming. Proposed tech kickoff: Mon 2026-03-22 at 10:00 AM PST — does that work for you?

Thanks,
